full_text:
In the newly renovated council chamber of the palace, King Krishnadevaraya had an ornate granite pillar installed, carved with images of celestial guardians.
A few weeks later, a chilling rumor spread among the ministers:
Whenever the King sat alone in the evening near the pillar, a faint, eerie, supernatural whisper echoed from the stone:
*‘Beware the Prime Minister... Trust only the Chief Treasurer...’*

King Krishnadevaraya, disturbed by the ghostly warnings, began to treat his faithful Prime Minister Appaji with cold suspicion, while promoting the dishonest Chief Treasurer, Devaraya.

Tenali Raman knew Prime Minister Appaji was incorruptible and suspected a treacherous conspiracy.
Tenali resolved to examine the whispering pillar.

Tenali waited until midnight, when the palace was quiet.
He entered the council chamber, lit a small oil lamp, and tapped the stone pillar with a small brass mallet from top to bottom.
At the height of six feet, the stone produced a slightly hollow, resonant ring!
Tenali examined the intricate stone carvings with a magnifying glass:
Beneath the carved ear of a celestial guardian, there was an almost invisible, paper-thin slit in the granite!

Tenali traced the direction of the pillar up to the ceiling.
Directly above the pillar was an ornamental false ceiling made of carved teakwood panels, leading to an attic storage gallery.

Tenali climbed into the dark attic above the chamber.
There, hidden beneath old rolls of carpets, Tenali found a long, hollow copper acoustic pipe, running from the attic floor straight down through the hollow core of the granite pillar to the tiny ear slit below!
Sitting on a stool beside the pipe, holding a speaking horn and waiting for the King’s evening prayer, was the Chief Treasurer’s confidential secretary!

Tenali gripped the secretary by his collar and marched him straight to the King’s private quarters!
Tenali brought the acoustic horn and exposed the mechanism before the Emperor:
'Maharaj! Behold your "celestial stone guardian"!
The pillar had no supernatural wisdom; it was merely an iron pipe through which a treacherous thief whispered poison to destroy an honest Prime Minister and seize control of the empire!'

King Krishnadevaraya was horrified and furious at his own gullibility.
He immediately restored Prime Minister Appaji to his full royal confidence, arrested the corrupt Chief Treasurer and his secretary, and had the hollow pipe dismantled.
The Emperor thanked Tenali Raman for preserving the integrity of the state against insidious deception.
moral: Supernatural whispers that manipulate royal decisions are traced to human conspirators hiding in the masonry. [ES]
